cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs from the Common Data Set (G1, which gives 2026-27 figures, and G5): tuition $64,703 (12-18 credits a semester; the same figure is on Pratt's 2026-2027 tuition page), required fees $2,024 (the cost-of-attendance PDF lists academic/activity fees $1,014, technology fee $610 and health services fee $400), on-campus food and housing $19,530 (housing $13,085 + meal plan $6,445), books and supplies $2,100, other expenses $2,369 (transportation 0 for residents). Pratt's 2026-27 cost-of-attendance PDF totals $90,967 for a resident, which also includes a $241 direct loan fee not shown in the CDS lines; international students pay a $100-a-semester international student service fee and a $100-a-semester activities fee (instead of $157). Health insurance is billed separately unless waived. The aid figures are CDS H6: 620 degree-seeking nonresident undergraduates received institutional scholarship or grant aid, average $19,224 (the CDS ticks both need-based and non-need-based boxes, but Pratt's scholarship page says international students do not qualify for need-based aid).

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (Fall 2025 entering class): 7,579 applied, 6,547 admitted (86.4%), 847 enrolled (the gender rows in C1 add up to these totals). The CDS covers the whole institute: Pratt's own Quick Facts brochure for fall 2025 excludes Munson (MWP) and shows 5,954 new-freshman applicants, 4,968 accepted and 757 enrolled, so those lower counts are not comparable with the CDS rows used here. Residency: admitted (in-state 1,375, out-of-state 3,214, international 1,958) and enrolled (183 / 481 / 183) rows add up to the totals, but the applicant rows (1,890 in-state, 4,201 out-of-state, 2,505 international) add up to 8,596, not 7,579, so the residency applicant counts are left blank rather than shown with an unreliable rate. Waiting list (C2): the CDS prints 1,001 offered a place, 139 accepting and 925 admitted, but more admitted than accepting is not possible, so only the offered count is kept. No early decision; early action is non-binding and non-restrictive (counts not asked). SAT/ACT percentiles are for enrolled first-years who submitted scores (132 students = 15.58% sent SAT, only 6 = 0.71% sent ACT, so the ACT range rests on very few students); Pratt is test-optional. GPA average 3.64 and the breakdown cover all enrolled first-years (100% reported); the 1.0-1.99 band is 0 and none had a GPA below 1.0. Undergraduate enrollment (3,734) and the nonresident count (884) are the CDS B1/B2 'Total Undergraduates' figures; the 8.9-to-1 student-to-faculty ratio is CDS I2 (4,792 FTE students).
